Subject: BCP evidence request: RTO/RPO and recovery procedures

Vanessa —

As part of our security/compliance review, we need a compact packet showing Redwood's current recovery capabilities for the managed inference platform. Specifically we are looking for:

- RTO and RPO numbers by product surface (API generation, embeddings, KV-store recoverability) with how those figures are measured (p50/p95 windows).
- Evidence of the most recent DR/exercise for region us-west-2 (date + short summary + postmortem).
- Warm-cache snapshot artifacts or a brief explanation of warm-start procedures (how long until full performance after failover).
- Retention policy for backups and a statement on point-in-time recovery (is PITR available / how is it implemented).

Can you provide the items above (PDF/excel or links) by EOD Monday 2026-06-22? Our compliance team wants to include this in the vendor risk assessment. If there are any limitations (e.g., not all surfaces have PITR), please call that out.

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. We can put together a focused packet that covers API generation, embeddings, and the KV/cache aspects. Attached in my follow-up will be the DR runbook (dr-runbook-v3.pdf), a compact RTO/RPO matrix (.xlsx) and a warm-cache snapshot export. High-level notes up front:

- Target RTOs: API-generation P50 ~ 40s, P95 ~ 160s for normal traffic shapes; embeddings P50 ~ 180s (due to batch-only paths), P95 ~ 420s (for large batches).
- RPO: user-facing persisted data is designed for <5 min (near-real-time replication). Cache/KV layers are best-effort; warm-cache snapshots shorten recovery but are not a guaranteed persistent store.
- Last full DR exercise: 2026-05-29 (we exercised failover to secondary region and validated end-to-end gen latency and data integrity). Postmortem will be included.

Before I assemble the packet, two quick clarifications so we provide exactly what you need:
1) Do you want raw artifacts (e.g., warm-cache snapshot files) or a redacted summary + checksums?
2) Are there specific SLAs/contract clauses that require signed attestation vs. a standard evidence packet?

If helpful I can propose a short review call tomorrow morning (30m) to walk through the artifacts.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-14T14:37:00-07:00

Vanessa — forwarding the thread and dropping the artifacts I prepared. See inline for key bullet answers so Alex has a concise summary for the compliance packet. Attachments in this email: redwood_rto_rpo_matrix.xlsx, warm-cache-snapshot-20260610.tar.gz, dr-test-postmortem-20260529.md

Key details (technical summary):
- API generation endpoints (production): measured with synthetic traffic from probe fleet. Typical numbers for service region us-west-2: P50 latency to first token ~ 40s under steady load; P95 to completion ~ 160s (depends on sequence length). RTO for control-plane orchestration and serving fleet rehydration is 3–8 minutes for baseline config to be back online; end-to-end request-level RTO (including data plane warm-up) is nominally 45s–7 minutes depending on cache state.
- Embeddings pipeline: batch-oriented; RTO measured as time to resume scheduled batch runs and clear ingestion backlog. Typical resumption window ~ 10–30 minutes; RPO is smaller (1–10 minutes) where ingestion is buffered and replayed.
- User data durability: primary metadata and customer content are replicated across AZs and asynchronously to a cross-region store. We guarantee RPO <5 minutes for persisted objects referenced in our agreement.
- Cache/KV: we do weekly warm-cache snapshots (binary export) and pre-warm flows post-failover. Warm-cache reduces tail latency during recovery; it is not a persistence guarantee — clients should treat cache as reconstructable. The attached warm-cache archive is a sanitized sample (no PII) showing keys and timestamped snapshot metadata.
- Backups & retention: automated nightly snapshots retained 30 days; critical customer artifacts retained 90 days per contractual addendum. PITR available for some control-plane metadata stores (Postgres WAL shipping), but not for accelerator-level ephemeral caches.
- DR exercise: 2026-05-29 — simulated primary region failover, cutover time 00:13:20 (start->validation) and full traffic rehydration by 00:42:00. Postmortem attached with findings and action items (dr-test-postmortem-20260529.md).

Notes on format: the Excel has a per-surface RTO/RPO table (numbers with measurement windows and methodology). The PDF runbook contains the step-by-step cold/warm start procedures. The warm-cache tarball is a small, redacted sample — we will provide checksums in the final packet.

Let me know if you want additional telemetry (traces/latency histograms) from the run — we can export a trimmed slice for auditors.

—Ben
